newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends lower on crude, sluggish demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends lower on crude, sluggish demand.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended modestly lower on Monday on the back of weaker crude oil futures and reluctant end-user demand, traders said.
Med prices were also under pressure as end-users chose to buy material from refiners due to the higher prices, one trader said.
But there were rumours that a major trader was getting a cargo together to send to the Far East, where prices have been steady, he said. This could not be confirmed.
Far East buying into the NWE swaps market also cushioned swaps prices early in the day, he said.
"I think basically that with the prices so high, refiners are producing naphtha and the end-users are taking it from them," this trader said.
March swaps ended $2.50 lower at $206.50/$207.50 a tonne after Brent futures lost near 40 cents at one point in late trading. April swaps fell $4 to $198/$199.
Cargoes were notionally assessed down $2 at $204/$208 cif NWE for prompt material.
